title: Majenius Move
summary: Recognize that extra blocked pawns can imprison their own king and force a pawn mate.

nodes.question: Can Black’s four pawns move safely?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...hxg6: White has Kf5/h3 against Kh5 and f6/g6/h6/h4. The earlier knight and bishop sacrifices remain source context outside this checked seven-piece tree.

branches.title: Force the only pawn to move
commentary: Begin in the complete seven-piece source diagram after the bishop and queen have disappeared.
Kxf6 removes the pawn that could otherwise move independently. The black king remains boxed in by its own pawns and White’s king.
g5 is Black’s only legal move, stepping the g-pawn forward.
Kf5 gains the opposition and controls g4/g5/g6 while preserving the mating capture.
g4 is again Black’s only legal move. Black must allow the h-pawn’s capture.
hxg4# is actual pawn mate. Kf5 protects g4 and covers g5/g6; Black’s own h4/h6 pawns block the remaining h-file flights.
branches.explanation: hxg4# is actual pawn mate. Kf5 protects g4 and covers g5/g6; Black’s own h4/h6 pawns block the remaining h-file flights.

branches.title: Let the king escape after the pawn push
commentary: Compare an independently supplied wrong king retreat after the forced pawn advance.
g5 is forced by the blocked position.
Ke5 abandons control of g6, releasing Black’s king from the mating net. The exact remaining pawn ending is a Black win with best play.

branches.explanation: Ke5 abandons control of g6, giving Black’s king an escape and losing the forced mating net. The exact outcome is checked rather than inferred from material.

exercises.prompt: Why take f6 before returning the king?
exercises.answer: Removing f6 leaves Black with only the g-pawn to move. Kf5 then turns that forced movement into a pawn mate.
